questions.questionText: A man bought a watch for ₹1200 and sold it for ₹1500. What is his profit percentage?
Find the LCM of 12 and 18.
A train travels at 60 km/hr for first half of journey and at 40 km/hr for second half. Find average speed.
questions.explanation: Average speed when distances equal = 2xy/(x+y) = 2×60×40/(60+40) = 4800/100 = 48 km/hr.

questions.questionText: The side of a square is decreased by 20%. Find percentage decrease in its area.
questions.explanation: Area ∝ side². New side = 0.8 times. New area = (0.8)² = 0.64 times. Decrease = 36%.
5 appears 4 times, more than any other number. So mode = 5.

questions.questionText: At what rate percent per annum simple interest will ₹3000 amount to ₹3600 in 3 years?
In a triangle, angles are in ratio 2:3:4. Find the largest angle.
questions.explanation: Sum of angles = 180°. Let angles be 2x, 3x, 4x. 2x+3x+4x = 9x = 180 → x = 20. Largest angle = 4x = 80°.

questions.questionText: A can do a work in 10 days, B in 15 days. They work together for 2 days, then A leaves. In how many days will B complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation: A's 1 day = 1/10, B's = 1/15. Together per day = 1/10+1/15 = 5/30 = 1/6. In 2 days, they complete 2×1/6 = 1/3. Remaining = 2/3. B alone needs (2/3)/(1/15) = 2/3 × 15 = 10 days.

questions.questionText: The average of 6 numbers is 25. If one number is excluded, average becomes 23. Find the excluded number.
questions.explanation: Sum of 6 numbers = 6×25 = 150. Sum of 5 numbers = 5×23 = 115. Excluded number = 150-115 = 35.

questions.questionText: Simplify: (2x+3)(x-4)
A man sells two fans for ₹2400 each. On one he gains 20% and on the other he loses 20%. What is overall gain/loss percentage?
If 4^(x-1) = 16, find x.
Find distance between points (1,1) and (4,5).
How many 5-letter words can be formed using letters of 'APPLE'?
questions.explanation: 'APPLE' has 5 letters with P repeated twice. Number of words = 5!/2! = 120/2 = 60.

questions.questionText: Three coins are tossed. What is probability of getting exactly two heads?
questions.explanation: Possible outcomes: HHH, HHT, HTH, THH, HTT, THT, TTH, TTT. Exactly 2 heads in 3 cases: HHT, HTH, THH. Probability = 3/8.

questions.questionText: Find derivative of cos x.
questions.explanation: d/dx[cos x] = -sin x.

questions.questionText: Find lim(x→1) (x³ - 1)/(x - 1).
Find ∫(x² dx).
questions.explanation: ∫x² dx = x³/3 + C.

questions.questionText: In how many ways can 5 people sit in a row of 5 chairs?
If tan θ = 3/4, find sin θ.
questions.explanation: tan θ = opposite/adjacent = 3/4. Hypotenuse = √(3²+4²) = 5. sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 3/5.

questions.questionText: Find determinant of [[5,3],[2,1]].
If f(x) = √x, find f'(4).
A card is drawn from a pack of 52 cards. What is probability it is a diamond or a face card?
questions.explanation: P(diamond) = 13/52, P(face card) = 12/52, P(diamond face card) = 3/52. P(diamond or face card) = 13/52 + 12/52 - 3/52 = 22/52 = 11/26.

questions.questionText: Find value of log₅ 25.
questions.explanation: 5² = 25, so log₅25 = 2.

questions.questionText: If P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A∪B) = 0.8, are A and B mutually exclusive?
questions.explanation: If mutually exclusive, P(A∪B) = P(A)+P(B) = 0.6+0.4 = 1. But given 0.8, so not mutually exclusive.

questions.questionText: Find sum of first 20 even numbers.
In a row of 60 students, Tom is 25th from left end. What is his position from right end?
questions.explanation: Position from right = 60 - 25 + 1 = 36.

questions.questionText: If 'BAT' is coded as 'CZW', how is 'CAT' coded?
questions.explanation: B→C (+1), A→Z (-1 or +25), T→W (+3). So pattern varies. For CAT: C→D (+1), A→Z (+25), T→W (+3) but not matching options. Let's assume reverse alphabet: B→Y, A→Z, T→G. Not matching. Perhaps BAT: B→C (+1), A→B (+1), T→U (+1) should be CBU. But given CZW. Actually B→C (+1), A→Z (-1), T→W (-3). So CAT: C→D (+1), A→Z (-1), T→W (-3) → DZW. Not in options. Let's use common +1 shift: C→D, A→B, T→U → DBU. That's option 1.

questions.questionText: M is N's mother. P is M's father. Q is P's wife. How is Q related to N?
questions.explanation: M is mother of N. P is father of M, so P is grandfather of N. Q is wife of P, so Q is grandmother of N.

questions.explanation: From statements, some animals are pets, so some pets are animals (II follows). But dogs may not be pets, so I doesn't necessarily follow.

questions.explanation: Only A = A - both = 60 - 30 = 30.

questions.questionText: If 'CODE' is coded as 'DPEF', how is 'DATA' coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifted by +1: C→D, O→P, D→E, E→F. So D→E, A→B, T→U, A→B → EBUB.

questions.questionText: At what time between 2 and 3 o'clock will the hands be at right angle?
questions.explanation: At 2:00, minute hand is 10 minutes behind hour hand. For right angle, difference should be 15 minutes. Relative speed = 11/2 min per min. Time = (10+15)/(11/2) = 25×2/11 = 50/11 = 4 6/11 min past 2. Also (10-15)/(11/2) = -5×2/11 = -10/11 (not valid). So first time = 2:27 3/11 approx.

questions.questionText: Find odd one out: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13
questions.explanation: All are prime numbers except 9 (which is 3×3).

questions.questionText: Pie chart shows income sources: Salary 50%, Business 30%, Investments 20%. If total income is ₹80000, what is income from Business?
If 'A % B' means A is father of B, 'A & B' means A is sister of B, 'A ^ B' means A is brother of B. What does 'P % Q & R' mean?

options.text: P is father of Q and Q is sister of R

questions.explanation: P % Q: P is father of Q. Q & R: Q is sister of R. So P is father of Q, and Q is sister of R, so P is also father of R (if R is child of P). But strictly, statement 1 is correct.

questions.explanation: Geometric progression: ×2 each time. 80×2 = 160.

questions.questionText: A shirt's price decreased from ₹800 to ₹640. What is percentage decrease?
questions.explanation: Decrease = 160. Percentage = (160/800)×100 = 20%.

questions.questionText: In a code, 'BLUE' is written as 'CMVF'. How is 'PINK' written?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifted by +1: B→C, L→M, U→V, E→F. So P→Q, I→J, N→O, K→L → QJOL.

questions.questionText: A person walks 12 km South, then turns left and walks 5 km, then turns left and walks 12 km. Where is he from starting point?
questions.explanation: South 12, left=East 5, left=North 12. Net displacement: 5 km East. Wait, East is option 1. Actually South 12, left=East 5, left=North 12. Net: East 5 km. So answer is 1.

questions.questionText: If 'MAN' is written as 'NBO', 'WOMAN' is written as 'XPNBO', how is 'CHILD' written?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifted by +1: M→N, A→B, N→O. So C→D, H→I, I→J, L→M, D→E → DIJME.

questions.questionText: Robot at (0,0) facing North. Commands: F=Forward, L=Left, R=Right. After FLFRF, where is robot?
questions.explanation: Start (0,0) North. F:(0,1), L:West, F:(-1,1), R:North, F:(-1,2). That's (-1,2). Not in options. Let's recalc: F(0,1), L:West, F(-1,1), R:North, F(-1,2). So (-1,2). Maybe option 2 is (-1,1) closest.

questions.questionText:
What does this algorithm do?
1. Input N
2. Count = 0
3. For i=1 to N
4.   If N % i == 0
5.     Count = Count + 1
6.   End If
7. End For
8. Print Count

options.text: Counts even numbers up to N
Counts odd numbers up to N

questions.explanation: Increments count when i divides N. So counts divisors of N.

questions.questionText:
Input: 12, 15, 8, 20, 10
Algorithm finds second largest. After comparing first 3 elements, what is current second largest?
questions.explanation: Initialize max=12, second=smallest. Compare 12 and 15: max=15, second=12. Compare 15 and 8: no change. So second largest after first 3 elements is 12.
Arithmetic progression: +3 each time. 15+3=18.

questions.questionText: If each letter is assigned its position (A=1, B=2,...), what is average of positions of 'MATH'?
Array: [9,5,7,3,1]. Algorithm sorts in ascending order using insertion sort (one pass). After inserting 3 into sorted part, what is array? (Assume sorted part initially [9], then [5,9], etc.)
questions.explanation: Insertion sort: Start with [9]. Insert 5: [5,9]. Insert 7: [5,7,9]. Insert 3: 3 compares with 9,7,5, inserts at beginning: [3,5,7,9]. Then array becomes [3,5,7,9,1].

questions.questionText: In a grid, numbers divisible by 3 are open paths. Robot at cell with value 5. Adjacent: North=6, South=9, East=7, West=8. Which direction can robot move?
questions.explanation: Divisible by 3: North=6 (yes), South=9 (yes), East=7 (no), West=8 (no). So can move North or South. North is option 1.

questions.questionText: Binary search on sorted array [2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16]. Searching for 10. How many comparisons until found?
questions.explanation: First mid: index 3 (value 8) <10, go right. Second mid: index 5 (value 12) >10, go left. Third mid: index 4 (value 10) found. So 3 comparisons.

questions.questionText: What is time complexity of bubble sort?
questions.explanation: Bubble sort has O(n²) time complexity.
